I'll check the intelligence databanks.|[[RC-1140/Legends|RC-1140]] and [[01/425]], upon sighting the ''Soulless One'' on Geonosis|<ref name="Republic Commando">''[[Star Wars: Republic Commando]]''</ref>}}
The '''''Soulless One''''' was the personal [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] of [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]], who used it during much of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] for the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], often when he would make his retreat from a doomed victory.

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|You know, integral hyperspace capability is rather useful in a starfighter; why don't ''we'' have it yet?|Obi-Wan Kenobi, lamenting the capabilities of Galactic Republic starfighters|<ref name="Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (novelization)">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref>}}
[[File:SoullessOne_ICS.jpg|thumb|left|180px|''Soulless One'' cross-section.]]
The ''Soulless One'' was a modified [[Belbullab-22 starfighter/Legends|Belbullab-22 starfighter]],<ref name="TCWCG" /> a fast and agile prong-shaped vessel produced by [[Feethan Ottraw Scalable Assemblies/Legends|Feethan Ottraw Scalable Assemblies]]. Grievous considered his fighter to be a vision of the future of warfare, with a powerful arsenal consisting of two sets of triple rapid-fire [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannons]]. The starfighter was easily able to match the [[Porax-38 starfighter]] for speed, fitted with twin [[Ion engine/Legends|ion drives]] and an extremely powerful [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]].<ref name="databank" />

Grievous modified his fighter with a top-of-the-line [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] allowing the [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] general to stay mobile on a [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]-wide scale. In order to remain in touch with his forces while flying his fighter, a powerful but compact [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]] transceiver was installed onboard, allowing Grievous to slice into legitimate and [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] networks.<ref name="databank" /> He also outfitted the ''Soulless One'' with a [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shield]], and had the entire hull coated in a thin layer of [[Impervium/Legends|impervium]], making the fighter impenetrable to all but the heaviest of enemy fire. The starfighter was originally designed for a biological pilot, and the one-pilot cockpit was equipped with a life-support system. This feature came in useful when [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], having destroyed Grievous on [[Utapau/Legends|Utapau]], appropriated the late general's starfighter, and used it to reach safe refuge aboard the [[Sundered Heart/Legends|''Sundered Heart'']].<ref name= "ROTS" />

==History==
[[File:SoullessOne.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Grievous used his starfighter, the ''Soulless One'', to flee the Battle of Geonosis.]]
After the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|first battle of the Clone Wars]], and the Confederacy's first defeat, Grievous used the fighter to secretly escape [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]], although it was seen by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] commandos of [[Delta Squad/Legends|Delta Squad]] and went unidentified at that time.<ref name="Republic Commando" /> During the [[Battle of the Kaliida Nebula/Legends|Battle of the Kaliida Nebula]], Grievous took the ''Soulless One'' to pursue the [[Twilight/Legends|''Twilight'']] but as the [[Malevolence/Legends|''Malevolence'']] crashed into the nearby moon, Grievous had to leave.<ref name="Destroy Malevolence">{{TCW|Destroy Malevolence|Destroy ''Malevolence''}}</ref>

Grievous also used the fighter as an escape ship on various missions. One such occasion was near the conclusion of the [[Battle of Bothawui/Legends|Battle of Bothawui]]. During the fight, Grievous' frigate sustained heavy damage and he was forced to flee. [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] spotted him and chased after the ''Soulless One'' in his [[Delta-7 Aethersprite-class light interceptor/Legends|Jedi starfighter]], detecting that Grievous' hyperdrive was activating and intent on preventing his escape. He shot at the ship continually, but Grievous proved to be a worthy pilot, rivaling even Skywalker, as he dodged every shot and escaped without a scratch.<ref name="Downfall of a Droid">{{TCW|Downfall of a Droid}}</ref>

Grievous later used the ''Soulless One'' to escape the crumbling [[Skytop Station/Legends|Skytop Station]] after a [[Raid on Skytop Station/Legends|skirmish]]. [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]] had managed to sever his right hand in a duel, but he managed to pilot the ship even with just his left hand.<ref name="Duel of the Droids">{{TCW|Duel of the Droids}}</ref> He also used it as a transport to his [[Grievous's castle/Legends|lair]], where its primary hangar was.<ref name="Lair of Grievous">{{TCW|Lair of Grievous}}</ref> Grievous and the fighter later appeared on [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]], where the commandos were able to get visual confirmation of the general and his fighter. However, Grievous' [[IG-100 MagnaGuard/Legends|IG-100 MagnaGuards]] spotted them and Grievous quickly used it to escape.<ref name="Republic Commando" />

In the last year of the Clone Wars, the ''Soulless One'' remained on a secret landing pad on the planet of [[Utapau/Legends|Utapau]]. After losing in a [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|lightsaber duel]] to [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], Grievous retreated to the secret landing pad closely followed by Kenobi. The two engaged in a fight and it ended when Obi-Wan shot Grievous dead. After [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]] was activated, Obi-Wan stole the fighter and used it to reach the [[Sundered Heart/Legends|''Sundered Heart'']].<ref name="ROTS" />

[[File:Belbullab22-SWCTP.png|thumb|right|250px|The ''Soulless One'' was commandeered by Obi-Wan Kenobi after Grievous' defeat.]]
The ''Soulless One'' remained in the ''Sundered Heart''{{'s}} docking bay until Kenobi used it to reach [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]], with the infant [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]]. There, the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Master]] sold the starfighter to [[Paolo's Chop Shop]] for passage to the planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] and credits for Skywalker's future caretakers.<ref name="Hyperspace">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/86/indexp2.html|text=The Story of General Grievous: Lord of War|int=The Story of General Grievous: Lord of War}}</ref>

The ''Soulless One'' was eventually tracked down by [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]] who was hunting Kenobi. After he anonymously reported the ''Soulless One'' to [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] authorities, the ship was brought to [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] secret storehouse on Utapau, where it was kept for use by [[N-K Necrosis]].<ref name="Hyperspace" /> When N-K Necrosis was destroyed by a group of [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] in [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], they took the ''Soulless One'' for themselves.<ref name="rotw" />

==Behind the scenes==
In the Decoded repeat of "[[Downfall of a Droid]]," when Grievous was escaping his frigate, ''Soulless One''{{'s}} name was revealed in one of the information bubbles, and it also comically stated that some Jedi might call it the "''Spineless One''," a reference to how Grievous has cowardly fled several battles with it.

In [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars|''The Clone Wars'' TV series]], the fighter has twin single-barrel laser cannons, whereas previous sources state that the fighter has twin triple-barrel laser cannons.
